title: Elderbot: A randomized controlled trial of a generative AI-based social interactive agent among older adults
summary:
The aim of this randomized controlled trial (RCT) is to evaluate the effectiveness, acceptance, safety, and usability of a large language model-based socially interactive agent (“Elderbot”). Elderbot was developed as a self-help intervention for older adults experiencing loneliness and provides social support as a competent conversational partner. In addition to loneliness, the current study examines the effects of Elderbot on users’ well-being, negative thoughts, psychological symptoms, and interest in social interaction.

Eighty older adults (N = 80; aged 60 years and older) who experience loneliness and live alone will be included in this RCT. At baseline, interviews will be conducted to collect sociodemographic and clinical data (e.g., the presence of mental disorders). Participants will complete questionnaires assessing loneliness (primary outcome) and other variables. Participants will be randomized to either the Elderbot group (n = 40) or a waiting-list control group (n = 40).

After a six-week intervention period (post; T1), the same questionnaires will be administered again. Additionally, participants in the Elderbot group will complete questionnaires assessing the user-friendliness and acceptance of Elderbot. Additional parameters, such as duration and frequency of use as well as the number of interactions, will be recorded. 

A final assessment will take place three months after T1 (follow-up; T2).

The results of this study will be used to examine whether use of Elderbot leads to a significant reduction in loneliness, improvements in well-being, reductions in negative thoughts and psychological symptoms, and increased interest in social interaction compared with a control group. We will further examine the extent to which participants rate Elderbot as useful and user-friendly.

interventions.name: Intervention group (IG): Participants in the IG receive access to Elderbot immediately after completion of the baseline assessment (T0) for a period of 6 weeks. A daily usage duration of 20 minutes is recommended, but no minimum or maximum usage duration is specified.
Waitlist Control Group (WL): Participants in the WL receive access to Elderbot after 18 weeks (at T2).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- relevant loneliness according to the total score on the UCLA-3 Item scale (UCLA-3 >5)
- lives in their residence alone (not institutionalized)
- adequate German language proficiency
- adequate cognitive functioning (MiniMoca = 10 or more)
- signed informed consent for participation
- willing to participate in the study and all assessments
Exclusion criteria:
- cognitive impairment / dementia 
- current inpatient or day clinic treatment
- Begin a new course of psychotherapy or medication for psychiatric symptoms (z.B. Sleep disorder, depression)
- The presence of the following diagnoses based on self-report or due to the Mini-Dips OA interview: current or past diagnosis of psychosis, bipolar disorder or borderline personality disorder, acute suicidality, current substance dependence, current social phobia, panic disorder or agoraphobia.
- Mobility limitations, which limit the ability to leave the place of residence
- Severe vision or hearing impairments or neurological disorders, which limit the use of the Elderbot
- more than infrequent use of Large Language Models (i.e., more than once per month)
- adequate distress tolerance
- absence from home for several days (e.g., due to vacation or extended travel) in which the Elderbot cannot be used.
